<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build and packaging process for the Draco 3D library from its official upstream source at https://github.com/google/draco. The source is fetched via Git using a tagged release (`#tag=${pkgver}`), which corresponds to the declared version 1.5.9. While the `sha256sums` array uses 'SKIP', this is common and acceptable for VCS-based sources in AUR packages, especially when referencing a specific tag, as it avoids checksum mismatches due to Git metadata. The build process uses CMake with standard secure installation prefixes and build flags, enabling shared libraries and release mode without any suspicious compiler options.

No network operations, file manipulations, or execution of external scripts occur outside the expected build flow. The package installs into `$pkgdir` using `make install`, which is standard practice. All dependencies are legitimate build and runtime requirements (cmake, git, glibc, etc.), and no obfuscated commands, eval usage, or data exfiltration attempts are present. The maintainer metadata is minimal but valid.

The use of `git+https` with a tag ensures reproducibility for this version, and while a commit hash would be more secure than a tag (which can be moved), this is not inherently unsafe—only a minor hygiene concern. There is no evidence of malicious behavior, backdoors, or supply chain attacks.
</details>
<evidence>
